title: Multi-tenant order and inventory API with EF Core
name: Tenant order reservations

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code keeps tenants' data separate? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A user from tenant A calls GET /api/orders/{number} with the number of an order that belongs to tenant B. What does the endpoint return?
choices: 403 Forbidden, because the tenant check fails after the row is loaded
The order, because Number is unique and the query matches it
404 Not Found, because the global filter removes the other tenant's order from the query, so it looks as if it does not exist
500, because SingleOrDefaultAsync throws when two tenants have the same order number

questions.prompt: What does the SaveChangesAsync override guarantee for entities that implement ITenantOwned?
choices: New rows are always written with the current tenant's id and existing rows cannot be moved to another tenant, regardless of what handler code sets
Reads of tenant-owned entities are filtered by the current tenant even when the query is a no-tracking query
Each SaveChanges call runs in a separate database transaction per tenant
It prevents two tenants from using the same SKU

questions.prompt: The Product filter reads _tenant.TenantId through the DbContext instance instead of capturing the tenant id as a local value in OnModelCreating. Why does that matter?
choices: It makes the filter run in memory instead of in SQL
It allows the filter to apply to AsNoTracking queries
It avoids a circular reference between Product and Order

EF Core builds and caches the model once per context type, so a captured value would freeze the first tenant's id; referencing the context member makes the id evaluated for each context instance when the query runs
